raw_case_text:
A 38-year-old Caucasian man presented a rash for 1 month that involved the face, trunk, and upper limbs. He was compliant with arthralgias, myalgias, asthenia, new onset stypsis, and mild anorectal pain. He reported his last sexual intercourse about 18 months ago, and he had self-healing genital and palmoplantar lesions more than 1 year ago. He denied any sexual relationship during the last 18 months, including oral sex and protected sexual intercourse, and he had never used illicit drugs. Physical examination showed two ulcerative lesions on the lips, painless bilateral cervical lymph nodes, and hyperkeratosis papules on the face, behind the left ear, on the neck, palms, soles, and scrotum (Fig. 1). A macular rash was in the trunk; erosive lesions were on the glans. Papular lesions were mild itching, and some of them were treated previously with cryotherapy for suspicion of common warts. He was afebrile, and his vital parameters were normal. Exams were all unremarkable but ALT (61, reference < 50 U/L). Treponemal test, rapid plasma reagin (RPR) for syphilis and serology for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) were ordered. Testing for HIV returned positive with a CD4 count of 385 (16.96 %, CD4/ CD8 = 0.3), HIV viral load of 43,400, and negative HIV p24 antigen. Syphilis serology was positive, with an elevated RPR titer of 1:128. A diagnosis of mucocutaneous relapse during untreated late latent syphilis with HIV coinfection was made. Molecular panel for sexually transmitted infection (Trichomonas vaginalis, Neisseria gonorrhoeae, Mycoplasma genitalium, Chlamydophila trachomatis) on first-void urine and rectal swab was negative. Screening for opportunistic infections, including tuberculosis (Quantiferon Tb Gold), cryptococcosis (serum antigen), toxoplasmosis (serology), and leishmaniasis (serology and polymerase chain reaction) was unremarkable all but positive Toxoplasma gondii IgG serology.
The patient was treated with three doses of 2.4 million units of benzathine penicillin administered 1 per week. Antiretroviral therapy with a bictegravir-based regimen was started concurrently with the first administration. Macular rash of the trunk, glans erosions, anorectal pain, and stypsis disappeared after the first dose of penicillin. The other lesions had a progressive improvement in the next three weeks.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 38-year-old Caucasian man presented with a 1-month history of a mildly pruritic papular and macular rash over his face, trunk, palms, soles, and genitalia, accompanied by arthralgias, myalgias, asthenia, constipation, and mild anorectal pain.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: One month prior to presentation, the patient developed hyperkeratotic papules on his face, retroauricular area, neck, palms, soles, and scrotum (some previously treated with cryotherapy as suspected common warts), along with a truncal macular rash, lip ulcers, glans erosions, arthralgias, myalgias, fatigue, new-onset constipation (stypsis), and mild anorectal pain.
subjective.past_medical_history: Reported his last sexual intercourse approximately 18 months prior to presentation, followed >1 year ago by self-healing genital and palmoplantar lesions. Denied any sexual contact over the past 18 months and denied illicit drug use.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for mildly pruritic mucocutaneous rash, lip ulcers, arthralgias, myalgias, asthenia, constipation, and mild anorectal pain; negative for fever.

objective.physical_examination: Vital signs were normal and the patient was afebrile. Cutaneous and mucosal examination revealed two ulcerative lesions on the lips, painless bilateral cervical lymphadenopathy, hyperkeratotic papules on the face, left retroauricular region, neck, palms, soles, and scrotum, a macular rash over the trunk, and erosive lesions on the glans penis.
objective.routine_investigations: Routine blood tests were unremarkable except for mildly elevated ALT at 61 U/L (reference <50 U/L). HIV serology was positive with an HIV-1 viral load of 43,400 copies/mL and negative HIV p24 antigen. First-void urine and rectal swab multiplex PCR for Trichomonas vaginalis, Neisseria gonorrhoeae, Mycoplasma genitalium, and Chlamydia trachomatis was negative. Opportunistic infection screening (QuantiFERON-TB Gold, serum cryptococcal antigen, Leishmania serology/PCR) was negative except for positive Toxoplasma gondii IgG.
objective.advanced_workup: CD4 T-lymphocyte count was 385 cells/mm3 (16.96%, CD4/CD8 ratio 0.3).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Confirmed mucocutaneous relapse of untreated late latent syphilis (secondary relapse) with newly diagnosed HIV-1 co-infection, established via positive treponemal test and high-titer serum RPR (1:128). Treated with intramuscular benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units once weekly for 3 consecutive weeks alongside concurrent initiation of bictegravir-based antiretroviral therapy. The truncal macular rash, glans erosions, anorectal pain, and constipation resolved after the first penicillin dose, and the remaining hyperkeratotic papules progressively cleared over the subsequent 3 weeks.
